ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a Zener diode voltage regulator circuit, where the input voltage Vin passes through the series resistor R and then reaches the output node; between this output node and the lower reference terminal, the Zener diode Dz and the load resistor RL are connected in parallel. The output voltage V0 is marked across the load, the load current IL=10 mA flows downward through RL, and the series resistor current divides at the output node into the load current and the Zener current. Reasoning: To ensure that the Zener diode still enters the voltage regulation region under the most unfavorable condition, when Vin is at its minimum value of 30 V, the Zener current should be at least equal to the knee current IZK=1 mA. Given V0=VZ=10 V, the voltage drop across the series resistor R is Vin(min)-V0=30-10=20 V. At this time, the resistor current must be at least IL+IZK=10 mA+1 mA=11 mA, therefore 20/R >= 0.011 A. Solving gives R <= 20/0.011 = 1818 Ω, and by conventional value selection it is approximately R <= 1.8 kΩ, namely R <= 1800 Ω.

The resistor has voltage drop Vin(min) - V0 = 30 - 10 = 20 V, so require 20/R >= 11 mA. Thus R <= 20/0.011 = 1818 ohms, conventionally stated as R <= 1.8 kΩ or R <= 1800 Ω.
